source: ORIGINAL EXAMS – Dự đoán đề Speaking quý 1/2023 (part 1 samples, gộp đề part 2)

speaking.title: Gộp đề 1 · An important text message / a photo you are proud of

questions: What do you usually do at weekends?
What did you do last weekend?
Do you like weekends?
Do you think it is important to make the most of your weekend?
samples: It largely depends on whether I'm tired. After a hard week I usually sleep in and stay in bed half the day doing nothing that involves much brainwork. If I don't feel like a squeezed lemon, I meet friends and we walk in the park or chat over coffee.

To tell the truth, I don't love weekends, because it's the only time I can do all my household chores, such as cooking and cleaning. But sometimes I dedicate time to my hobbies or visit my parents out of town.

I believe it's essential to rest properly at the weekend, because we aren't robots and our brain can't work non-stop at the same productivity. Weekends are a kind of system reboot, after which you feel rested and energetic.

questions: What kinds of music do you like to listen to?
When did you start listening to that type of music?
Do you often listen to music?
How do you feel when you listen to it?
samples: I'm a music lover, so I enjoy different genres, because any music – classical, electronic or pop – creates feelings in my soul. Classical music lessens my stress, whereas rock evokes strong memories.
I started listening to pop at a very early age, I guess around five or six. As for rock, I fell in love with it in my early twenties after hearing the Rolling Stones' 'Paint It Black'.
It seems I listen to it all the time – while working, driving, cooking, working out and even lying around. I can say I listen to music my entire day.
I feel elated when I listen to music I like. I just melt into the melody and flow with the rhythm. It makes me relaxed, pumped up and really blissful.

part2.topic: Describe an important text message you received
part2.cue: Describe an important text message you received
points: what you did after receiving it
and explain why it was important to you
followUp: Describe a website you often visit
Describe an advertisement you don't like
Describe a photo you took that you are proud of
Describe a time when you forgot/missed an appointment
Describe a time you made a decision to wait for something
Describe a long walk you had
part2.sample:
I was just about to head out to an appointment when I received an important text message from my friend. She told me that she had booked a surprise trip for us to Japan through Agoda, a travel agency. I was ecstatic and couldn't wait to embark on this adventure. I immediately went to Agoda's website to check the details, but as I was browsing, I came across an advertisement I didn't like: it was for a 'luxury' resort that looked more like a cheap, run-down hotel. The pictures were misleading and the reviews were poor, so I decided to wait for a better deal.

I ended up forgetting about my appointment and missed it. I felt guilty, but I knew I had made the right decision. My patience paid off – we booked the trip at a much better rate and had an amazing time in Japan.

One of the highlights was a long walk through the beautiful city of Kyoto. We wandered through traditional gardens and saw the most beautiful temples and shrines. I took a photo of my friend and me standing in front of a traditional Japanese gate – the colours and details were so beautiful, and it's a moment I will always treasure.

The trip was a great success, and I was glad I had waited for the perfect deal. I would recommend Agoda to anyone planning a trip, but I'd advise them to be patient and not to be swayed by misleading advertisements.

questions: How has communication changed since text messaging became popular?
Do you think people rely too much on their phones?
Why do some advertisements annoy people?
Should advertising aimed at children be restricted?
Is it better to wait for something or to act immediately?

speaking.title: Gộp đề 2 · A new development in your area / plastic waste

questions: Do you mind noise?
Do any noises bother you?
Are cities becoming noisier?
What types of noise do you come across in your daily life?
Are there any sounds that you like?
samples: I'd say I'm pretty tolerant of noise when I'm awake, as I've learned to cut out unwanted sounds. But when I'm about to fall asleep I become very sensitive – even the muffled sound of a slammed door next door can make me toss and turn all night.
There's no worse noise than chalk scraping on a blackboard. Even the thought of it makes me feel sick.

Yeah, the level of noise is getting higher and higher – so high it's now regarded as a form of environmental pollution. Cities are more crowded, there's more traffic, and air-conditioning units are a huge part of ambient noise.

Splashing waves and the cries of seagulls sound like music to me. I also enjoy the sound of rain when I'm inside, and the clanking of train tracks, which sends me to sleep as soon as the train leaves.

questions: Do you prefer buying things from big companies or small businesses?
Do you know many small businesses?
samples: Definitely from small businesses. First, they do their best to stay competitive on price; second, they're more likely to offer good customer service, since every deal and review matters to them. And when I buy locally, I cycle money back into my community.

Yeah, there are lots where I live – pizza parlours, coffee shops, barber shops and small retail outlets. Many people prefer to start small businesses because they want the freedom to fill niches with more innovative products.

part2.topic: Describe a new development in the area where you live (e.g. a shopping mall, a park)
part2.cue: Describe a new development in the area where you live (e.g. a shopping mall, a park)
points: how long it has been there
and explain how you feel about it
followUp: Describe a time when you saw a lot of plastic waste (e.g. in a park, on the beach)
Describe a problem you had while shopping online or in a store
Describe a place you visited that has been affected by air pollution (or is not clean)
part2.sample:
A new shopping mall has just opened in my neighbourhood in Hanoi, and it was a much-needed addition to the area. The mall is modern and spacious, with a wide variety of shops and restaurants. It's great to finally have a place like this nearby, and it has brought a lot of new job opportunities and businesses.

However, as I was walking around the mall, I noticed something alarming. There was a lot of trash, particularly plastic waste, scattered throughout the building and the surrounding streets. The management had not put proper measures in place to manage the waste, and it was affecting the environment. The plastic waste was not only unsightly but also a health hazard to visitors and the local community. The stench of garbage was overwhelming, and it was hard to enjoy the shopping experience.

I noticed later that the management had started to take steps to reduce the litter. They set up recycling bins and designated collection points, launched an awareness campaign to educate visitors about not littering, and employed staff to make sure the trash was disposed of properly.

The mall has brought a lot of benefits to the local economy, but it is clear that the environmental impact needs to be addressed. The management should be more proactive in managing the waste so that the mall is not only a great place to shop but also a clean and safe environment for the community.

questions: What are the advantages and disadvantages of building large shopping malls in residential areas?
Who should be responsible for reducing plastic waste – individuals, businesses or governments?
Why do people continue to use plastic even though they know it is harmful?
How can cities reduce air pollution?

speaking.title: Gộp đề 3 · Overcoming difficulties / a difficult decision

questions: What made you happy when you were a child?
What makes you happy now?
samples: When I was a child, I felt happy every time I went to the seaside with my family, playing in the water and building sandcastles. Another thing was doing little experiments to learn how things work. And, of course, receiving the presents I wanted – I must admit gifts still make me happy.

questions: Do you go to sleep early or stay up late?
How do you feel in the morning after you stay up late?
What were you doing when you stayed up late last time?
samples: Well, I normally go to bed at about 10 p.m., as I believe there's no point sacrificing sleep for other activities. However important they seem, the benefits won't outweigh the harm sleep deprivation does to my health.
You know, I'm like a zombie the next day. I drink coffee non-stop, but it doesn't help much, and that overcast feeling follows me until night-time.
Last Sunday I promised myself I'd go to bed before midnight, but I binge-watched an entire season of a series and ended up going to bed at 4 a.m.

part2.topic: Describe a time when you overcame difficulties in doing something and succeeded
part2.cue: Describe a time when you overcame difficulties in doing something and succeeded
points: and explain how you felt about succeeding
followUp: Describe a positive change that you made in your life
Describe a difficult decision that you made and had a good result
Describe a disagreement you had with someone
part2.sample:
For as long as I can remember, my parents wanted me to become a doctor. They pushed me to excel in science and maths and had planned my future since I was a child. But deep down, I knew it wasn't my passion. I had always been interested in law and the idea of fighting for justice. I never had the courage to tell them, because I was afraid of disappointing them and losing their support.

As the university entrance exam approached, I knew it was now or never. I couldn't go through with a career I had no passion for – it would be a waste of time and energy. So I decided to pursue my dream of becoming a lawyer and tried to persuade my parents. It was a difficult conversation and we had a real argument. I explained my reasons and how much it meant to me, but they thought I was throwing away my potential. I stood my ground, because I knew I had to be true to myself.

Eventually, after a lot of talking, my parents saw how determined I was and gave me their approval. It was a bittersweet moment – a huge relief, but also a reminder of how hard it is to go against their wishes.

Deciding to study law was a positive change in my life. It has allowed me to pursue my passion and brought a sense of fulfilment I never thought possible. My parents, who were unhappy at first, have now seen the positive impact and are proud of my decision. I am following my heart and studying what I love, and I'm excited about the future.

questions: What kinds of difficulties do young people face when choosing a career?
Should parents have a say in their children's career choices?
Why are some people afraid of change?
How can people learn to handle disagreements constructively?

When did you start listening to that type of music?
Do you often listen to music?
How do you feel when you listen to it?
samples: I'm a music lover, so I enjoy different genres, because any music – classical, electronic or pop – creates feelings in my soul. Classical music lessens my stress, whereas rock evokes strong memories.
I started listening to pop at a very early age, I guess around five or six. As for rock, I fell in love with it in my early twenties after hearing the Rolling Stones' 'Paint It Black'.
It seems I listen to it all the time – while working, driving, cooking, working out and even lying around. I can say I listen to music my entire day.
I feel elated when I listen to music I like. I just melt into the melody and flow with the rhythm. It makes me relaxed, pumped up and really blissful.

questions: Do you like art?
Have you ever visited an art gallery?
samples: Oh yeah, I do. I always get a warm feeling when I look at artworks. It's interesting to figure out the hidden symbolism, and art helps me forget my worries – the moment I immerse myself in a painting, my thoughts change for the better.

part2.topic: Describe an impressive English lesson you enjoyed
part2.cue: Describe an impressive English lesson you enjoyed
points: when and where you had it
and explain why you enjoyed it
followUp: Describe a song or a piece of music you like
Describe a movie you watched recently and would like to watch again
Describe a story or novel you have read that you found interesting
part2.sample:
I recently had an English lesson in which my teacher played the movie 'The Hunger Games'. The film is set in a dystopian society where children are forced to fight to the death in a brutal annual event. As I watched the story unfold, I felt a mix of emotions: anger towards the oppressive government, fear for the innocent children, and hope for the protagonist, Katniss, as she fought for survival and rebellion. It was intense and thought-provoking, and I was engrossed from start to finish.

One of the most memorable parts was the song 'The Hanging Tree', which features in the film. It was haunting and stayed in my mind long after the movie ended. The lyrics, the melody and the way it was used gave me a sense of rebellion and a longing for freedom.

The movie was so interesting that I decided to buy the book and read it at home. The novel gave me a deeper understanding of the story and its themes, and I was even more impressed after reading it. It was a powerful reminder of the importance of standing up for what is right and the strength of the human spirit.

I hope teachers will introduce more works like this to students. It's a great way to engage us in critical thinking, encourage us to explore important themes, and inspire us to think more deeply.

questions: Do you think films are a good way to learn a language?
Why do some people prefer books to films?
How has the way people listen to music changed?
Should schools teach more literature?

part2.topic: Describe an interesting old person you met
part2.cue: Describe an interesting old person you met
points: what you did or talked about
and explain why you think this person is interesting
followUp: Describe a person who inspired you to do something interesting
Describe a person you have met who you want to work/study with
Describe a person you met at a party who you enjoyed talking with
Describe a person you know who is from a different culture
part2.sample:
I met a 60-year-old British teacher at a school orientation event. He introduced himself as a retired careers counsellor from Huddersfield University. He was charming, with a warm smile, and I felt drawn to him immediately. We started chatting and he asked about my plans for the future.

I told him about my parents' dream for me to become a doctor, and that my real passion was law. He listened carefully and understood my predicament. He encouraged me to follow my own dreams and not let anyone else dictate my future, and told me it was important to pursue what makes me happy and fulfilled.

He shared his own story: he had followed his passion for teaching despite his family's expectations that he become a lawyer. He said it was the best decision he had ever made, and that he loved being able to inspire and guide young people.

I was touched by his words and his real interest in my future. After talking with him, I felt more confident and determined to pursue my dream of becoming a lawyer. I hope to work with him one day and to inspire other young people the way he inspired me.

questions: What can young people learn from older people?
Do older people in your country receive enough respect?
Why do some people find it easy to talk to strangers?
Is it important to have a mentor in your career?

speaking.title: Gộp đề 6 · A childhood friend / someone who dresses well

questions: Do you usually wear T-shirts?
Do you like wearing T-shirts?
samples: Yeah, I do. A T-shirt is always a good choice. They're super comfy, usually made of cotton, which is one of the most skin-friendly fabrics, and they're versatile – I can dress them up or down depending on the occasion.

questions: Have you ever given someone jewellery as a gift?
Do you like wearing jewellery?
samples: Oh yeah, I've done it a couple of times. Both pieces were for my best friend, who lives abroad these days – I just wanted to let her know that I care and put a smile on her face.

part2.topic: Describe a friend from your childhood
part2.cue: Describe a friend from your childhood
points: and explain why this friend is memorable
followUp: Describe a character in a film or TV show
Describe a person who likes to dress fashionably/well
part2.sample:
My childhood friend Quỳnh Liên is three years older than me. Growing up, she was always interested in fashion and make-up. Despite that, her parents wanted her to go to college and become a lawyer or a doctor, but she found it irrelevant and dropped out after a few semesters.

Quỳnh Liên decided to pursue her passion and created her own fashion channel on YouTube. She shared fashion and make-up tips and tutorials, and quickly gained a following. Her talent and creativity made her famous and allowed her to earn a lot of money.

She was always trying to recreate items from high-end fashion houses such as Gucci and Dior. She was very skilful and it was inspiring to see her work. Later she became a host of Vietnam's Next Top Model, where she could share her passion and inspire other young people in the industry.

Quỳnh Liên did not follow her parents' dream, and she always encouraged me to do the same. She said it was important to pursue what makes you happy and not to let anyone dictate your future. She is living proof that following your dreams can lead to success and happiness. Her example helped me a lot, because like her, I don't want to become a doctor as my parents wish, but a lawyer instead.

questions: Why do people lose touch with childhood friends?
Is it important to dress well at work?
How has social media changed the fashion industry?
Do you think people judge others by their clothes?

part2.topic: Describe a popular place for sports (e.g. a stadium) that you have been to
part2.cue: Describe a popular place for sports (e.g. a stadium) that you have been to
points: and explain how you felt about this place
followUp: Describe a place you would like to visit for a short time
Describe a noisy place you have been to
part2.sample:
I went to a football match between Thailand and Vietnam at My Dinh Stadium. The atmosphere was electric from the moment I stepped inside. Fans were cheering and shouting, holding up banners and flags, and the noise was overwhelming – but exciting at the same time. It was the final of the AFF tournament, a big deal for both countries, and Vietnam hadn't won the championship for a long time, so the excitement was palpable.

I went with my parents, who are both big football fans. We had been looking forward to the match for weeks, and it was a great way to release the stress of studying. We found our seats and settled in among passionate, enthusiastic supporters.

The match itself was intense and thrilling. Both teams played with skill and determination, and the score remained close throughout. My heart was racing as the clock ticked down, and the final whistle blew with the score tied. It was a hard-fought draw, but the atmosphere was simply amazing.

Although I loved the atmosphere, I wouldn't go there too often. The stadium is always crowded, there's no air conditioning so it gets stuffy and hot, and tickets and food are quite expensive. But the experience was worth it. I had a wonderful time with my parents, cheering on the Vietnamese team, and it was a great way to bond and forget about exams for a while.

questions: Why do people enjoy watching sport live rather than on TV?
Should governments spend money building large stadiums?
How does noise affect people's health?
Are there enough quiet places in modern cities?

speaking.title: Gộp đề 8 · A place to relax at home / a home you often visit

questions: Do you usually carry a lot of keys with you?
Do you often forget to take your keys when you go out?
Have you ever lost any keys?
Do you think it's a good idea to leave a key to your home with a neighbour?
samples: Yes, I carry quite a few: my room key, the key to my building, my locker key at school and my gym locker key, all on one chain with other random keys.
I rarely forget them, since there are so many I need every day. It would be a disaster if I left them at home.
Only once, when I was about twelve. My parents had just entrusted me with my first set of house keys, I left them in a park, and I was severely told off.
Personally, I don't think it's a good idea. It's more important to be responsible with your keys and self-reliant rather than bothering the neighbours when you're locked out.

questions: How often do you visit a library?
Would you ever like to work in a library?
Did you use a library more when you were younger?
How common is it for children to visit libraries in your country?
samples: Very frequently. I'm in the middle of my studies, constantly writing essays and preparing for exams, so I'm in the library almost every day. My friends say I practically live there!
I could see myself working in a library one day. I'm a studious person who loves books, and libraries are relaxing places where the job isn't stressful.
Not really. When I was growing up I spent most of my time watching TV or playing video games with friends, so I didn't read much. Now, as a student, I spend far more time in libraries.
I think it's very common. We have a strong culture of hard work and self-improvement, so many parents take their children to libraries to foster good reading habits and broaden their horizons.

part2.topic: Describe the home of someone you know well and that you often visit
part2.cue: Describe the home of someone you know well and that you often visit
points: and explain how you feel about this home
followUp: Describe your favourite place in your house where you can relax
Describe a house or apartment you would like to live in
part2.sample:
My favourite place in my grandma's house is her garden. It's a peaceful, serene spot where I can relax and unwind after a long day. The garden is filled with beautiful flowers and lush green plants; the sweet fragrance of the blooms fills the air and the birdsong creates a soothing atmosphere.

There's a small pond in the centre with a little bridge over it, where I like to sit and watch the fish swimming. The sound of water falling from the fountain is calming and relaxing.

My grandma has a small bench under a big old tree where she likes to sit and read. I often join her and we chat about our day or about life in general.

The garden is surrounded by tall walls that give a sense of privacy, making it the perfect place to escape the hustle and bustle of daily life. I always look forward to spending time there – it's a special place that brings me a lot of peace and joy, and it holds many happy memories for me.

questions: What makes a house feel like a home?
Do people prefer living in houses or apartments in your country?
Why do some people find it hard to relax at home?
How important are gardens and green spaces in cities?

part2.topic: Describe a sport you enjoyed when you were young
part2.cue: Describe a sport you enjoyed when you were young
points: and explain why you enjoyed it
followUp: Describe a routine you have in your life that you enjoy
Describe something that you did with one or more people
Describe an outdoor activity you did in a new place recently
part2.sample:
After school, my best friend Quỳnh Liên and I often play badminton at the local park. We've been playing together for years, and it's one of our favourite things to do. We always bring our own rackets and shuttlecocks and play for hours.

We enjoy the competition and the feeling of hitting the shuttlecock back and forth. We often switch between doubles and singles, so we can improve our skills in different ways.

Not only is it a fun way to spend time together, it's also good for our physical health. We get a great workout, and it helps us stay in shape and improves our hand-eye coordination and reflexes.

Playing badminton is also a great stress reliever. We can forget about our problems and just focus on the game, laughing and joking around. It's a great way to bond and strengthen our friendship, and we've created a lot of happy memories.

Unfortunately, the university entrance exam is right around the corner, so we've had to put it on hold. After the exam, though, we'll definitely have a rematch.

questions: Why is sport important for children?
Do you think competition in sport is good for young people?
Why do people's routines change as they get older?

speaking.title: Gộp đề 10 · A place to recommend / a historical period

questions: Do you want to travel in outer space?
What would you do if you had the opportunity?
Have you ever learnt about stars and outer space?
Is it important to study stars?
samples: Of course I do. I love space and I'm sure travelling there would be an incredible experience – floating around, discovering new planets. I'd really love to try it.
If I had the opportunity, I'd definitely take it, as I've dreamt about space travel since childhood. I know the training would be enormous and it could be dangerous, but I'd still seize the chance.
Yes, once. It was an online course I took last summer about the distant past and future of the Earth, the Sun and our universe, and I was satisfied with what I learnt.
I'm sure it is. Stars help us understand how our solar system was formed and give a lot of information about the physical world, so studying them is really important.

questions: Do you like art?
Have you ever visited an art gallery?
samples: Oh yeah, I do. I always get a warm feeling when I look at artworks. It's interesting to figure out the hidden symbolism, and art helps me forget my worries – the moment I immerse myself in a painting, my thoughts change for the better.

part2.topic: Describe a place in your country that you would like to recommend to visitors
part2.cue: Describe a place in your country that you would like to recommend to visitors
points: who you would recommend it to
and explain why you would recommend it
followUp: Describe a historical period you would like to know more about
Describe an unusual meal you had
part2.sample:
I recently travelled to Hue, the ancient capital of Vietnam. It's located in the central part of the country and is known for its rich history and culture. I was excited to explore this beautiful city and see all the palaces and historical landmarks it has to offer.

As soon as I arrived, I visited the Imperial City, the palace of the last emperors of Vietnam. The architecture was stunning, and I was fascinated by the intricate details of the buildings. I also visited the Forbidden Purple City, which was the residence of the royal family.

Next I went to the Thien Mu Pagoda, a historic Buddhist temple dating back to the 17th century. It sits on the banks of the Perfume River, and the view was beautiful. I also saw the tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty emperors, set in peaceful grounds surrounded by lush gardens.

One of the highlights of my trip was the Citadel, a large fortress built to protect the city from invaders. It was impressive to see how well preserved it is and to learn the history behind it.

I also had the chance to try the local cuisine, which was delicious and varied, and I met some friendly locals who gave me great recommendations. I would recommend Hue to anyone interested in history, architecture and good food.

questions: Why is it important to preserve historical sites?
Do you think tourism damages historical places?
How can people learn about history apart from at school?
Why are some people not interested in history?
Do you like chocolate?
Did you like chocolate when you were a child?
Have you ever given chocolate as a present to someone?

Definitely. I don't think there's a kid in the world who doesn't enjoy chocolate. I adored that melt-in-the-mouth feeling every time I popped a piece into my mouth, and I always waited for chocolate surprises from anyone visiting our place.
Millions of times, actually. It's a traditional present on Valentine's Day, symbolising affection and passion, and it's also a perfect 'thank you' gift for colleagues, friends and teachers.

samples: Well, I normally go to bed at about 10 p.m., as I believe there's no point sacrificing sleep for other activities. However important they seem, the benefits won't outweigh the harm sleep deprivation does to my health.
You know, I'm like a zombie the next day. I drink coffee non-stop, but it doesn't help much, and that overcast feeling follows me until night-time.
Last Sunday I promised myself I'd go to bed before midnight, but I binge-watched an entire season of a series and ended up going to bed at 4 a.m.

questions: Do you want to travel in outer space?
What would you do if you had the opportunity?
Have you ever learnt about stars and outer space?
Is it important to study stars?
samples: Of course I do. I love space and I'm sure travelling there would be an incredible experience – floating around, discovering new planets. I'd really love to try it.
If I had the opportunity, I'd definitely take it, as I've dreamt about space travel since childhood. I know the training would be enormous and it could be dangerous, but I'd still seize the chance.
Yes, once. It was an online course I took last summer about the distant past and future of the Earth, the Sun and our universe, and I was satisfied with what I learnt.
I'm sure it is. Stars help us understand how our solar system was formed and give a lot of information about the physical world, so studying them is really important.

questions: Have you ever given someone jewellery as a gift?
Do you like wearing jewellery?
samples: Oh yeah, I've done it a couple of times. Both pieces were for my best friend, who lives abroad these days – I just wanted to let her know that I care and put a smile on her face.

questions: What kinds of music do you like to listen to?
When did you start listening to that type of music?
Do you often listen to music?
How do you feel when you listen to it?
samples: I'm a music lover, so I enjoy different genres, because any music – classical, electronic or pop – creates feelings in my soul. Classical music lessens my stress, whereas rock evokes strong memories.
I started listening to pop at a very early age, I guess around five or six. As for rock, I fell in love with it in my early twenties after hearing the Rolling Stones' 'Paint It Black'.
It seems I listen to it all the time – while working, driving, cooking, working out and even lying around. I can say I listen to music my entire day.
I feel elated when I listen to music I like. I just melt into the melody and flow with the rhythm. It makes me relaxed, pumped up and really blissful.

questions: Do you prefer buying things from big companies or small businesses?
Do you know many small businesses?
samples: Definitely from small businesses. First, they do their best to stay competitive on price; second, they're more likely to offer good customer service, since every deal and review matters to them. And when I buy locally, I cycle money back into my community.

Yeah, there are lots where I live – pizza parlours, coffee shops, barber shops and small retail outlets. Many people prefer to start small businesses because they want the freedom to fill niches with more innovative products.

questions: What do you usually do at weekends?
What did you do last weekend?
Do you like weekends?
Do you think it is important to make the most of your weekend?
samples: It largely depends on whether I'm tired. After a hard week I usually sleep in and stay in bed half the day doing nothing that involves much brainwork. If I don't feel like a squeezed lemon, I meet friends and we walk in the park or chat over coffee.

To tell the truth, I don't love weekends, because it's the only time I can do all my household chores, such as cooking and cleaning. But sometimes I dedicate time to my hobbies or visit my parents out of town.

I believe it's essential to rest properly at the weekend, because we aren't robots and our brain can't work non-stop at the same productivity. Weekends are a kind of system reboot, after which you feel rested and energetic.

questions: Do you usually wear T-shirts?
Do you like wearing T-shirts?
samples: Yeah, I do. A T-shirt is always a good choice. They're super comfy, usually made of cotton, which is one of the most skin-friendly fabrics, and they're versatile – I can dress them up or down depending on the occasion.

questions: What made you happy when you were a child?
What makes you happy now?
samples: When I was a child, I felt happy every time I went to the seaside with my family, playing in the water and building sandcastles. Another thing was doing little experiments to learn how things work. And, of course, receiving the presents I wanted – I must admit gifts still make me happy.

questions: Do you like art?
Have you ever visited an art gallery?
samples: Oh yeah, I do. I always get a warm feeling when I look at artworks. It's interesting to figure out the hidden symbolism, and art helps me forget my worries – the moment I immerse myself in a painting, my thoughts change for the better.

questions: Do you mind noise?
Do any noises bother you?
Are cities becoming noisier?
What types of noise do you come across in your daily life?
Are there any sounds that you like?
samples: I'd say I'm pretty tolerant of noise when I'm awake, as I've learned to cut out unwanted sounds. But when I'm about to fall asleep I become very sensitive – even the muffled sound of a slammed door next door can make me toss and turn all night.
There's no worse noise than chalk scraping on a blackboard. Even the thought of it makes me feel sick.

Yeah, the level of noise is getting higher and higher – so high it's now regarded as a form of environmental pollution. Cities are more crowded, there's more traffic, and air-conditioning units are a huge part of ambient noise.

Splashing waves and the cries of seagulls sound like music to me. I also enjoy the sound of rain when I'm inside, and the clanking of train tracks, which sends me to sleep as soon as the train leaves.

questions: Do you usually carry a lot of keys with you?
Do you often forget to take your keys when you go out?
Have you ever lost any keys?
Do you think it's a good idea to leave a key to your home with a neighbour?
samples: Yes, I carry quite a few: my room key, the key to my building, my locker key at school and my gym locker key, all on one chain with other random keys.
I rarely forget them, since there are so many I need every day. It would be a disaster if I left them at home.
Only once, when I was about twelve. My parents had just entrusted me with my first set of house keys, I left them in a park, and I was severely told off.
Personally, I don't think it's a good idea. It's more important to be responsible with your keys and self-reliant rather than bothering the neighbours when you're locked out.

questions: How often do you visit a library?
Would you ever like to work in a library?
Did you use a library more when you were younger?
How common is it for children to visit libraries in your country?
samples: Very frequently. I'm in the middle of my studies, constantly writing essays and preparing for exams, so I'm in the library almost every day. My friends say I practically live there!
I could see myself working in a library one day. I'm a studious person who loves books, and libraries are relaxing places where the job isn't stressful.
Not really. When I was growing up I spent most of my time watching TV or playing video games with friends, so I didn't read much. Now, as a student, I spend far more time in libraries.
I think it's very common. We have a strong culture of hard work and self-improvement, so many parents take their children to libraries to foster good reading habits and broaden their horizons.
